correctness.rationale: The recent finite-sign reduction turns the count into an exact k-dimensional lattice probability. Direct overlap counts give covariance limit B_k=(1/k)I+((k+2)/k^2)J with determinant (k+3)/k^k. Linear-sized coordinate-only sign blocks identify exactly 2^k Fourier peaks; parity makes their contributions equal. Gaussian expansion at those peaks yields the explicit constant and the square-root-scale exponential factor. Exact finite counts, covariance determinants, and parity checks agree with the formulas.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 Li--Xu--Yan preprint proves only two-sided correct order for fixed eventual difference and does not state a leading constant or square-root-scale Gaussian profile. The inspected surrounding weighted-representation literature concerns small-threshold exact formulas, structural existence, finite-group variants, or lower bounds on representation counts. No prior statement of the explicit constant or profile was located. The 2012 Yang--Chen paper was not fully inspected, and the motivating preprint is recent, so these are retained as residual originality risks.

value.rationale: The theorem upgrades a new correct-order result to a sharp asymptotic with closed constant, shows that every fixed eventual difference has the same leading term, and identifies the full central Gaussian profile. It also supplies a precise asymptotic ratio between the original Yang--Chen counting functions for different weights.
